key_insight: A single-run ADAPT-SSVQE quantum workflow can recover multiple nuclear shell-model eigenstates at once while preserving fermionic and angular-momentum symmetries.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the need for repeated excited-state searches and offers a path to tackle Hilbert spaces that are too large for classical full-matrix diagonalization.
method: Map the shell-model Hamiltonian from bits to qubits with Jordan-Wigner to preserve fermionic anti-commutation.
Use SSVQE with an adaptive single/double-excitation operator pool to optimize a weighted energy sum over a targeted M_J subspace.
Run one variational circuit to obtain mutually orthogonal low-lying states and intrinsically restore J^2 symmetry.
evidence_signal: In simulation, the approach benchmarked two- and three-particle cases in a j = 9/2 orbital, extracting 5 and 10 orthogonal states respectively within a 10-qubit active space and matching exact diagonalization closely.
watch_item: The results are demonstrated in simulation on small active spaces, so scalability to larger nuclei and noise-resilient hardware performance remains to be validated.
paper_title: Full-Spectrum Quantum Simulation for the Nuclear Shell Model
